clue.text: Intimidate tormentor, not unknown to go off

indicators.note: 'not' tells us to drop the letter an algebraic unknown stands for from the word before

parts.note: a tormentor of weaker people
y is an unknown quantity in algebra
to go off is to drop off to sleep

explanation.surface: A bully who keeps menacing until something snaps and they explode.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go off' looks like exploding, but here it means nodding off to sleep; in algebra the unknowns are x, y and z.
explanation.definitionFit: To bulldoze someone is to force or frighten them into giving way, a figurative synonym.

clue.text: Using pen, setter reported snooker?

parts.note: a pig pen

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so we go by how these words are heard

parts.note: the crossword setter refers to themself as me

explanation.surface: A puzzle setter, armed with a pen, reports on a game of snooker.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, STY plus ME is STYMIE. In snooker you snooker an opponent by leaving a ball in their way, which is just what a stymie does in old golf.
explanation.definitionFit: To stymie and to snooker both mean to block or thwart someone by putting an obstacle in their path.

clue.text: University study

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the University of ..., in the English town of that name
second meaning: the act of studying books

explanation.walkthrough: Reading is a town in Berkshire, west of London, with its own university; with a capital letter hidden by the clue's start, the word is also plain study.
explanation.definitionFit: Reading names a British university and also means the perusal of books, a kind of study.

clue.text: Help housing company in Detroit for backing old region

indicators.note: going backing means moving the opposite way, so the whole construction is read from right to left
a word housing another holds it inside like a building around its tenants

parts.note: aid is help
Tamla, later Tamla Motown, was the record company founded in Detroit

explanation.surface: Someone seeks help from a Detroit firm in exchange for financial backing.
explanation.walkthrough: AID holds TAMLA to give AITAMLAD, which read in reverse is DALMATIA, the old Adriatic coastal region now mostly in Croatia.
explanation.definitionFit: Dalmatia is a historic region on the Croatian coast, once a Roman province, so it is an old region.

clue.text: Keep scholar's book

parts.note: a don is a university scholar; the 's is read as 'has'
Jon is the abbreviation for the Book of Jonah

explanation.surface: An instruction to retain an academic's book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keep' looks like a verb but is the noun: the central tower of a castle.
explanation.definitionFit: A donjon is the great inner tower of a medieval castle, which is also called the keep.

clue.text: Right out of potato cake? Get mash

definitions.note: a whimsical description: one who sets out to win admirers

indicators.note: taking a thing out of something leaves that something without it

parts.note: a croquette is a fried cake of mashed potato
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A cookery query about potato cakes, then an instruction to mash the spuds.
explanation.walkthrough: CROQUETTE without its R leaves COQUETTE. 'Mash' is old slang for an admirer or a flirtation, so a coquette is one who gets a mash.
explanation.definitionFit: A coquette is a flirt who tries to win admiration, and mash is dated slang for a sweetheart or crush.

clue.text: Works round problems, primarily given time

parts.note: O is round in shape

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter of the word is wanted

parts.note: its first letter
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Someone tackles difficulties at work, given enough time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Works' is a noun here: OPERA is the Latin plural of opus, a work.
explanation.definitionFit: Opera is the plural of opus, a creative work, so it can stand for works as well as for sung drama.

clue.text: Evoke a flower in Yorkshire

parts.note: taken as written
R for river plus the Ouse, a Yorkshire river; a flower is something that flows

explanation.surface: A bloom growing in Yorkshire brings back memories.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is the crossword river, something that flows: here the Ouse, which runs through York, abbreviated with R for river.
explanation.definitionFit: To arouse a feeling or memory is to evoke it, call it up; the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Schoolgirl interpreted so quickly in Berlin

parts.note: the whole word as printed, read as two words, which is what 'interpreted so' asks
SCH is the standard abbreviation for school
a girl's name, as in Little Nell

explanation.surface: A schoolgirl translating something rapidly into German.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Interpreted so' tells you to read the single word Schoolgirl as its two parts, school and girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Schnell is the German word for fast or quickly, the sort of word you would hear spoken in Berlin.

clue.text: Lads regularly getting round in bar, causing pandemonium

indicators.note: in places the selected letters inside the following word

parts.note: a beam is a long bar of wood or metal

indicators.note: getting round is turning about, so the kept letters face the other way
regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: first and third letters

explanation.surface: Rowdy lads drinking rounds at the bar and creating chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Round' and 'bar' look like pub talk; one turns the letters, the other is a structural beam.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedlam, named after the old London asylum, has become a byword for uproar and wild confusion.

clue.text: Knocked back medium can, having consumed one bottle

indicators.note: what is consumed ends up inside, so a letter goes into the middle of the words
a drink knocked back goes the wrong way down, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: MED is the abbreviation for medium
the Roman numeral for one
both are slang for a lavatory

explanation.surface: Someone downs a medium-sized can after already drinking a whole bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can' is not a drink container but American slang for the toilet. The reversal applies only to the first word.
explanation.definitionFit: A demijohn is a large narrow-necked bottle, often wicker-covered, used for wine or home brewing.

clue.text: Emperor in north cut off, retreating after a long time

parts.note: the compass abbreviation

indicators.note: in says one piece sits inside another

parts.note: an aeon is an immensely long period

indicators.note: a word in retreat moves backwards, so it is written from its end

parts.note: to lop is to cut off a branch

explanation.surface: An emperor isolated in the north and retreating after many years, as in the march from Moscow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut off' looks like isolated, but it is the gardener's verb for pruning a branch.
explanation.definitionFit: Napoleon Bonaparte crowned himself Emperor of the French in 1804, so he is a famous emperor.

clue.text: Struck by flyweight after swapping sides?

indicators.note: swapping sides means the left and right halves change places before they are joined

parts.note: the boxing class as printed, read as its two halves
a ton is a unit of weight
a ked is a sheep tick, a wingless fly

explanation.surface: A boxer floored by a flyweight opponent after changing corners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flyweight' is split into fly and weight, which then swap order. To tonk is slang for hitting hard.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonked is informal British slang meaning hit hard or thrashed, so struck fits as a past tense.

clue.text: Just after turning back, first arrive at hell

parts.note: to infer is to arrive at a conclusion

indicators.note: something turning back faces the opposite direction, so the word is written in reverse

parts.note: as in 'on the stroke of midnight'

explanation.surface: Instructions for a traveller who turns round and lands somewhere hellish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First' tells you which piece leads; 'arrive at' as in arriving at a conclusion, with 'at' a joining word.
explanation.definitionFit: Inferno is the Italian word for hell, made familiar by the first part of Dante's Divine Comedy.

clue.text: Reach up above aerial, oddly a long drop from here?

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means reading from the bottom, so the word is reversed

parts.note: to gain a place is to reach it

indicators.note: oddly keeps the letters in odd-numbered positions

parts.note: first, third and fifth letters

explanation.surface: Climbing up past an antenna to a height from which it would be a long fall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Above' places the reversed word on top of the selected letters in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Niagara Falls on the US-Canada border is famous for its great plunge of water, a long drop indeed.

clue.text: Flowers, ones thus having managed to climb

indicators.note: climbing in a down entry means going up the column, so the letters read bottom to top

parts.note: I's, more than one I, the Roman numeral one
Latin for thus, used in quotations
to run a business is to manage it

explanation.surface: Flowers that have succeeded in growing upwards like climbing plants.
explanation.walkthrough: The three pieces are joined and the whole string read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Narcissi is the plural of narcissus, the spring flower family that includes the daffodil.

clue.text: Run garlic sauce around very small pasta

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for a run

indicators.note: a sauce around something surrounds it, holding that letter inside

parts.note: aioli is garlic mayonnaise
very is cut small to its abbreviation

explanation.surface: A recipe: pour garlic sauce round little pasta parcels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very small' is not a size: it shrinks the word very to its abbreviation V, which goes inside AIOLI after R.
explanation.definitionFit: Ravioli are small square pasta parcels with a filling, so they are a kind of pasta.

clue.text: Temporary officer replacing a single means of exchange?

indicators.note: replacing says one piece is swapped in where another one stood

parts.note: interim means temporary
commanding officer
I is one, a single

explanation.surface: A temporary officer standing in for someone, as though money were being exchanged.
explanation.walkthrough: In INTERIM the second I gives way to CO. 'Exchange' hints at a telephone exchange; the question mark flags the playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An intercom lets people talk to each other between rooms, so it is a means of exchanging words.

clue.text: Remove harness from stunned couple

parts.note: knocked out cold
a span is a pair, as of horses or oxen

explanation.surface: Unharnessing a pair of dazed horses.
explanation.walkthrough: Outspan is a South African word from Afrikaans for unyoking oxen from a wagon.
explanation.definitionFit: To outspan is to unyoke or unharness draught animals, the opposite of inspan, a South African term.

clue.text: Bone meat and cut nothing more

indicators.note: cut takes something away, so a letter is removed from the word that follows

parts.note: ham is cured pork
O looks like zero
taken as written

explanation.surface: A butcher's instruction: bone the joint and stop cutting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bone' looks like the butcher's verb but is a noun; MORE loses its O.
explanation.definitionFit: The hammer, or malleus, is one of the three tiny bones in the middle ear, so it is a bone.

clue.text: One to one at Buck House?

definitions.text: One to one at Buck House?

parts.words: One to one at Buck House?
parts.note: surface reading: a private one-on-one meeting at Buckingham Palace

parts.words: One to one at Buck House?
parts.note: setter's reading: what the word one means to a royal, who uses one for I or me

explanation.walkthrough: Buck House is slang for Buckingham Palace. Royals are famous for saying 'one' instead of I, so to the Queen 'one' means the reflexive first person.
explanation.definitionFit: When royalty says one, they mean themselves, the first-person reflexive pronoun, so the royal 'one' translates to it.

clue.text: Relax strike in disheartened association

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other
losing heart means losing the central letter of the word

parts.note: a union is an association
to butt is to strike with the head

explanation.surface: A demoralised trade union decides to relax its strike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strike' and 'association' call up an industrial walkout, but the strike is a blow with the head.
explanation.definitionFit: To unbutton is informally to loosen up and relax, as one undoes a collar to get comfortable.

clue.text: Overlooking chap bitten by insect

indicators.note: something bitten has jaws closed around it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a bee is an insect
a man's name

explanation.surface: A man stung by a bug while gazing at the view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overlooking' is not about ignoring something: a house overlooking the sea stands beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A cottage beside the river overlooks it, so beside works as a preposition for overlooking.

clue.text: Had expressed disapproval following father's departure

indicators.note: after the departure of something it is no longer there, so those letters are removed

parts.note: a frown shows disapproval
Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest

explanation.surface: Someone frowned at bad behaviour after Dad had walked out.
explanation.walkthrough: FROWNED loses FR.
explanation.definitionFit: Had in the sense of possessed: if you owned something, you had it.

clue.text: Cases girl mostly going round with diamonds, say

indicators.note: going round something encircles it, so the other pieces sit inside

parts.note: a lass is a girl
W is the abbreviation for with

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: diamonds is one suit of cards, an example

explanation.surface: A girl wearing plenty of diamonds, perhaps to court.
explanation.walkthrough: LAS wraps around W and SUIT. 'Cases' means court actions, not luggage.
explanation.definitionFit: Lawsuits are legal actions brought before a court, which lawyers call cases.

clue.text: Economical, suppressing a rise

indicators.note: suppressing something keeps it out of sight, so that letter is taken away

parts.note: sparing means frugal
taken as written

explanation.surface: A thrifty employer holding back a pay rise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rise' looks like a pay increase, but it is the verb: to spring up. SPARING loses its A.
explanation.definitionFit: To spring is to rise or leap up suddenly, as water springs from the ground.

clue.text: Poles eating cored fruit in port

indicators.note: what is eaten goes inside, so the fruit sits between the two letters

parts.note: north and south, the two magnetic poles

indicators.note: coring a fruit removes its centre, so the middle letter goes

parts.note: an apple is a fruit

explanation.surface: Polish sailors snacking on apples in a harbour town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' are not Polish people but the ends of the globe; APPLE loses its central P.
explanation.definitionFit: Naples is a major Italian seaport on the Bay of Naples, hence a port.

clue.text: Radio broadcast about new, extremely devious robots

indicators.note: about means around, so the scrambled word encloses the next letter
broadcast scatters things widely, so the letters are strewn into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes, the first and last letters

parts.note: its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A radio programme about sneaky new robots.
explanation.walkthrough: The new letter sits after the first letter of the rearranged word, and the two extremes of devious follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Androids are robots built to look and act like humans, a science-fiction staple.
